title: Chapter 274: Fatal Message [2 in 1]
html:
At 11:34 p.m., while Chen Ge was still in the police car, Captain Yan called.

“The situation is deteriorating. Our opponents are alert and may have detected us.” Captain Yan sent Chen Ge a photograph. “When our investigator entered the elevator, he found a phone inside. This unfinished message was on its screen.”

The photograph showed Xiao Gu’s phone. A strange passage filled the composition field.

“Daddy killed us and laid us on the stairs.

“Big brother is lying behind me.

“Little brother is lying in front of me.

“Can you find us?”

“What does this mean?” Chen Ge frowned at the unfinished message, unable to grasp what it described.

“I suspect they detected us and deliberately left the message where we would find it.”

“Your teams already entered Building Three?” Chen Ge had warned Captain Yan against drawing attention.

“Neither plainclothes team has entered Fang Hwa Apartments. Their vehicles are parked at an intersection roughly 150 meters away. They’re ready and awaiting orders.”

“Then how could anyone discover you? Did the scout make a mistake?”

“Impossible. The investigator scouting Building Three is a senior officer with seven years of experience. He has helped solve cases others considered impossible.” Captain Yan trusted his people. “Besides, the phone was waiting when the elevator opened. Placing it unseen would require at least three minutes, and three minutes earlier, our teams had not entered the complex.”

“I understand. The suspects placed the phone before you arrived.” Realization changed Chen Ge’s expression. “Where is the investigator who found it?”

“Still inside Building Three. He sent the photograph.”

“Damn it! Order him out immediately!” The Ghost Stories Society had trapped Xiao Gu to lure in Chen Ge. The strange message was almost certainly intended for him too.

His many encounters had taught Chen Ge certain rules. Most ghosts, even Red Specters, required a medium to affect the physical world: Zhang Ya’s love letter, Xu Yin’s tape, the Pen Spirit’s ballpoint pen. Conversely, ordinary people needed such ‘special items’ to trigger contact with the other side.

The message on Xiao Gu’s phone was likely such a trigger. Anyone who read it became the target of one or more unknown ghosts.

“Understood.” Captain Yan requested no explanation. He immediately ordered the investigator to withdraw, only to discover that the man had already stopped responding.

“This is bad!” Captain Yan did not hang up, so Chen Ge could hear him clearly.

“I’m three or four minutes away. Do not send anyone else inside!”

Officers discussed options on the other end. Seconds later, Chen Ge heard a door open and someone address Captain Yan. After a brief exchange, the captain ordered the newcomer to remain in his vehicle and returned to the call. “The investigator’s trainee just reported that his instructor sent him a WeChat message.”

“But the investigator wouldn’t answer your call.” Chen Ge’s attention sharpened. “What did the message say?”

“Only three words—Are you there?”

“Are you there?”

“The investigator did not send that.” Captain Yan’s voice hardened. “An experienced officer would never send a meaningless question to his trainee during an operation. If he needed help or encountered danger, he would contact the commander first.”

Something has already happened to him.Chen Ge kept the thought to himself.

“Whatever happened, we’ll assume the worst.” With an investigator potentially in mortal danger, Captain Yan could no longer wait outside. “Contact Teams One and Two. Move immediately. Enter Building Three!”

“Captain Yan, don’t rush in. The people hiding there are extremely dangerous!”

“The situation has changed. We have no choice. Give the phone to Officer Wu and have him bring you here.”

Lives were at stake, and Chen Ge knew persuasion would fail. He compromised. “Keep the trainee who received that message away from the building. He may already have been targeted.”

Something happened after the investigator read Xiao Gu’s message; immediately afterward, his trainee received the strange question. The sequence felt significant. Chen Ge recalled Xiao Gu’s truncated call. His first words had concerned Uncle Wong.

Chen Ge organized the clues. After beginning work at the Haunted House, Xiao Gu had little reason to return to Fang Hwa Apartments for a night patrol. Why had he entered Building Three?

This must involve Uncle Wong. Perhaps Xiao Gu received a message from his account too.Chen Ge tried to warn Captain Yan, but the captain had ended the call to command his teams. Three minutes later, the police car reached Fang Hwa Apartments.

“Have you found the missing investigator?”

“Yes. We found him near the stairs to the second floor. He appears physically unharmed but remains unconscious. The officers who recovered him said his gaze was vacant and his face deathly pale.” Standing beside the police vehicles with a radio in hand, Captain Yan frowned deeply. “How did anyone incapacitate a healthy, combat-trained man within minutes?”

As they spoke, a medical team brought out the investigator. Chen Ge examined his clothes. Unless someone removed his shirt and exposed the police undershirt beneath, he looked like any ordinary resident. Discovering his identity should not have been easy.

“The Ghost Stories Society probably mistook him for a civilian who wandered into its trap. They treat human lives as disposable and show no restraint toward innocents. This time, however, they made a grave mistake.”

During Chen Ge’s first visit to the twenty-fourth floor, Zhu Xiu had asked the Ghost Stories Society to help him evade the police. The society refused outright. That detail proved something important: its members dared not confront law enforcement openly. They were rats infesting the city’s shadows, spreading chaos and decay but terrified of the light.

“Captain Yan, what happened to the phone in the elevator? Did your people recover it?” The question was crucial. The Ghost Stories Society had left the unfinished message as a trap, and merely viewing it could invite disaster.

“Team One recovered it. It’s sealed in an evidence bag.” Captain Yan did not understand the danger, but Chen Ge did. Too many lives were at stake to waste another second. “Captain Yan, I’m their true target. I won’t let anyone else suffer in my place.”

Then, he walked toward Fang Hwa Apartments.

“Wait.” Captain Yan would have stopped any ordinary civilian, but Chen Ge was different. He retrieved a radio from a vehicle and handed it over. “Do you know how to use this?”

“Yes. When the Haunted House had more employees, everyone carried one.”

“Good.” Still concerned, Captain Yan summoned Officer Wu, who had driven Chen Ge. “Enter together. Each of you can watch the other’s back.”

Chen Ge accepted the precaution and entered Fang Hwa Apartments with Officer Wu. To prevent panic, Captain Yan had not warned the residents, and Building Three remained eerily silent. Dim light washed over unnaturally white walls as the two men approached the elevator.

“Captain Yan wants us behind Team Two, so we’ll go straight to the fifth floor.” Officer Wu confirmed both teams’ positions over the radio. “Stay behind me, and do not wander away.”

Bringing a victim along to apprehend the culprit was exceedingly rare. Given everything surrounding Chen Ge, however, Officer Wu soon accepted it. In three weeks, the man beside him had filled an entire row of filing cabinets at the Serious Crimes Unit. The thought made Officer Wu edge away instinctively.

“Officer Wu, we need to find Team One first. That phone is dangerous, and they may already be in trouble.” Every delay increased the risk.

“No. Captain Yan explicitly ordered us to follow Team Two.”

“We’ll only check on Team One. If they’re safe, we’ll rejoin Team Two.”

“All right.” After a long hesitation, Officer Wu entered the elevator with Chen Ge and selected the eighth floor. “Teams One and Two are clearing opposite stairwells. Team One is moving faster and therefore faces greater danger. Captain Yan assigned us to Team Two because he doesn’t want you taking unnecessary risks.”

“I understand,” Chen Ge answered distractedly. As the numbers climbed, his gaze kept returning to the button that should not exist—24. They soon reached the eighth floor.

Team One had already reached the ninth floor, clearing levels at impressive speed. Officer Wu contacted its leader, and the two men entered the emergency stairwell to meet them.

They waited until Team One’s leader and two officers emerged from the corridor. “Why did you bring him?”

Team One’s leader was large and muscular. He had sat across from Chen Ge during the interrogation. Captain Yan had called him Lee Zheng.

“Captain Yan ordered it.” Officer Wu glanced at the men beside Lee Zheng. “Why are there only three of you?”

“Xiao Jia and Ah Cheng are guarding the corridor’s far end so no suspect slips past while we search.” Lee Zheng looked behind him. “Strange. Didn’t you pass them on the way up?”

A terrible feeling seized Chen Ge. “Do they have the phone recovered from the elevator?”

“Yes. Why?” Lee Zheng already knew Chen Ge’s reputation, even before that evening’s interrogation. Then understanding struck. He frowned, raised his radio, and shouted down the poorly lit corridor, “Xiao Jia! Ah Cheng!”

His booming voice echoed away. After a long delay, the radio crackled. “Brother Zheng, something is wrong with Xiao Jia. He keeps running upstairs and won’t answer me. We’re on the fourteenth floor—I just caught him… Xiao Jia! What are you doing? Have you lost your mind?”

Chaos erupted over the radio, followed by the impact of something heavy hitting the floor.

“Ah Cheng?” Lee Zheng tightened his grip on the radio and led the remaining officers upstairs. Chen Ge and Officer Wu followed. On the fourteenth floor, they found Ah Cheng sprawled on the ground with both hands covering his face. Blood seeped between his fingers.

“Officer Wu! Take Ah Cheng downstairs immediately.”

“Brother Zheng, I’m fine. Find Xiao Jia—he looks possessed!”

Lee Zheng gently pulled back Ah Cheng’s fingers. A deep bite marked his cheek, and the backs of his hands bore large wounds.

“Does Xiao Jia have the phone?” Chen Ge was the calmest person present. “Did either of you read the message on it?”

“I didn’t. Xiao Jia glanced at it before sealing the phone in the evidence bag,” Ah Cheng answered.

I knew it. The message triggered this.Chen Ge reviewed its peculiar wording. Daddy killed us and laid us on the stairs. That points toward the stairwell, but what do the brothers positioned before and behind each other mean? And why does it end by asking the reader to find them?

While Chen Ge considered the riddle, Lee Zheng led his men to the fifteenth floor.

“Officer Wu, stay with Ah Cheng. I’ll investigate.” Before the officer could object, Chen Ge sprinted upstairs. The first investigator who read the message collapsed, but Xiao Jia became violent. What caused the difference?

Lee Zheng wished to keep his group together, but searching floor by floor was the only way to intercept Xiao Jia. Chen Ge had a different priority. From the fifteenth floor, he entered the elevator and selected twenty-three—the level Xiao Gu had named and therefore the likeliest center of danger. I hope Xiao Gu is still alive.

As the elevator doors closed, Chen Ge kept one finger on the recorder’s play button. Alone, he might have fallen into the Ghost Stories Society’s trap. This time, the police gave him the numerical advantage.

The numbers climbed. At the twenty-first floor, Chen Ge’s phone vibrated.

He opened the notification and found a message from Xiao Gu’s account.

“Are you there?”

Chen Ge replied immediately.

“Send me your location. I’m coming for you.”
